title: Connection and termination
summary: Describes how different cables are terminated and the main types of accessory terminal: square, circular, moving plate, insulation displacement and post.

sections.heading: Termination of cables
paragraphs: Each cable has its own method of termination. Some cables require specialist tools, and MICC requires a number of specialist tools. Thermoplastic cables (PVC twin and earth and singles) can be terminated with the standard tools.
bullets: Each cable has its own method of termination
MICC requires a number of specialist tools
Thermoplastic cables: PVC twin and earth and singles

sections.heading: Types of accessory terminal
paragraphs: When terminating cables into an accessory, take into account the type of terminal being used. Most accessories use a grub screw which is screwed down onto the conductor to keep it in place.

sections.heading: Square and circular terminals
paragraphs: Square terminals are used in accessories such as socket outlet face plates, where two or even three cables can be terminated in the same terminal. Problems arise if the conductor is not doubled over.
Circular terminals are found in accessories such as light switches and ceiling roses, where single or small cables are terminated.
bullets: Square: socket outlet face plates; two or even three cables in the same terminal; conductor should be doubled over
Circular: light switches and ceiling roses; single or small cables
Circular bottom terminals position the conductor directly beneath the terminal screw, so there is no need to bend the end of the conductor over

sections.heading: Moving plate, insulation displacement and post terminals
paragraphs: Moving plate terminals are often used on protective devices such as circuit breakers and fuse holders mounted in consumer units and distribution boards.

Insulation displacement is common in the telecoms part of the industry and is used where the conductor is so small that a screw-type terminal is impractical. The post terminal looks like an upturned screw.
bullets: Moving plate: circuit breakers and fuse holders in consumer units and distribution boards
Insulation displacement: telecoms; very small conductors
Post terminal: looks like an upturned screw
Post terminal: conductor is wound around it in a clockwise direction or fitted with a cable crimp lug
